ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: It has often been noted that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons having extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite distinct kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for cultivating the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen." So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is willing to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has eaten the oysters. The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.

questions.passage: It has often been ①<u>noted</u> that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons ②<u>having</u> extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite distinct kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, ③<u>departing</u> from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for cultivating the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have ④<u>seen</u>." So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is willing to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has eaten the oysters. The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ departing → apart (apart from은 전치사구로 '~와 별도로'라는 의미이므로 departing은 불가)
det.analysis:
✅ ① noted: 'It has often been noted that ~'에서 현재완료 수동태의 과거분사로 올바른 어법
✅ ② having: 'persons having extraordinary memories'에서 현재분사가 persons를 수식하는 분사구문으로 올바른 어법
❌ ③ departing → apart: 'the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance'에서 apart from은 관용 전치사구(~와 별도로). departing from은 동사구(~에서 떠나다)로 문맥과 구조가 맞지 않음 ←정답
✅ ④ seen: '"Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen."'에서 현재완료의 과거분사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 'apart from'은 '~와 별도로, ~을 제외하고'라는 의미의 관용 전치사구입니다. departing from은 '~에서 떠나다'라는 동사구로 여기서 대체할 수 없습니다.

So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is ③<u>willing</u> to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has ④<u>eaten</u> the oysters. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① which → who (선행사가 The man of genius(사람)이므로 관계대명사 who가 필요)
det.analysis:
❌ ① which → who: 'The man of genius, which may have no special reason'에서 선행사가 사람(The man)이므로 관계대명사 who가 와야 함. which는 사물에 사용 ←정답
✅ ② cultivating: 'for cultivating the lower kind'에서 전치사 for 뒤에 동명사로 올바른 어법
✅ ③ willing: 'he is willing to let the words ~ go'에서 형용사 보어로 올바른 어법
✅ ④ eaten: 'after he has eaten the oysters'에서 현재완료의 과거분사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 'The man of genius, who may have ~'에서 선행사가 사람이면 who, 사물이면 which를 씁니다.

det.korean: ④ differing → differs (주절의 주동사가 필요하므로 현재분사 differing이 아니라 동사 differs가 와야 함)
det.analysis:
✅ ① distinct: 'two quite distinct kinds of memory'에서 형용사로 명사 kinds를 수식하여 올바른 어법
✅ ② retains: 'his heart retains the significance'에서 3인칭 단수 주어에 호응하는 동사로 올바른 어법

det.tip: 'The well-informed person commonly differs from ~'에서 differs는 주절의 주동사입니다. differing으로 바꾸면 주어에 동사가 없어집니다.

det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② triviality(사소함) → significance(중요성)
det.analysis:
✅ ① extraordinary(비범한): 비범한 기억력을 가진 사람이라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② triviality(사소함) → significance: 마음이 사실의 '중요성(significance)'을 유지한다는 원문인데 triviality(사소함)는 정반대 ←정답
✅ ③ willing(기꺼이 하는): 단어와 사실을 기꺼이 보내준다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ burden(짐): 영혼이 짐 아래 여위었다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 'retains the significance'에서 significance(중요성)는 천재가 사실의 표면이 아닌 핵심 의미를 간직한다는 뜻입니다. triviality(사소함)는 정반대입니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ obstacle(장애물) → help(도움)
det.analysis:
✅ ① noted(언급되다): 천재가 기억력이 나쁘다고 '언급되어 왔다'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② principles(원리): 정신적 사실과 '원리'에 대한 기억이라는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ obstacle(장애물) → help: 'find it rather a hindrance than a help'에서 도움(help)이라기보다 방해가 된다는 대조 구조. obstacle(장애물)은 hindrance와 같은 의미이므로 대조가 성립하지 않음 ←정답
✅ ④ thin(여윈): 영혼이 짐 아래 여위었다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 'rather a hindrance than a help'에서 hindrance(방해)와 help(도움)은 대조됩니다. obstacle(장애물)로 바꾸면 hindrance와 obstacle이 같은 의미가 되어 대조가 깨집니다.

questions.passage: It has often been noted that men of genius have bad memories, and that persons having extraordinary memories, like Cardinal Mezzofanti, have little else. The truth is that there are two quite distinct kinds of memory: the memory for external facts and words, apart from their significance; and the memory for spiritual facts and principles. The man of genius, who may have no special reason for cultivating the lower kind of memory, may even find it rather a hindrance than a help. His prayer is, "Let not my heart forget the things my eyes have seen." So long as his heart retains the significance of the facts he has seen and the words he has heard, he is willing to let the words and the facts go, as a man casts away the shells after he has eaten the oysters. The "well-informed" person commonly differs from the man of genius in this: that he carries about with him all the shells of all the oysters he has ever eaten, and that his soul has grown thin under the burden.
